findings.title: Split reviews record only the first part’s spend
findings.description: Each part receives usage, but `fold_review_parts()` copies only the first part’s metadata. Subsequent parts’ tokens, turns, duration, and cost disappear before persistence. Reproduced with two parts costing $1 and $2: the folded record reports $1. Aggregate all parts’ usage and add a split-review accounting test.

findings.title: Run totals omit earlier loop iterations
findings.description: The report reads only persisted `action_results`. The executor keeps earlier iterations in `StepResult.prior_rounds`, but `StateManager._append_step()` serializes only the final iteration’s `action_results`; the round observer records nothing. Consequently, retry/revision loops report only their last round’s spend. Preserve earlier rounds durably and test totals across multiple iterations.

findings.title: Fan-out usage is discarded during reduction
findings.description: Capture reaches each branch, but the persisted result contains only the reducer output. `CollectReducer` drops branch metadata, `FirstPassReducer` also omits usage, and failed branches produce an empty action list. Reproduced a successful collect reduction returning empty metadata despite priced branch records. Preserve every branch’s spend independently of which output wins reduction.

findings.title: Standalone subscription reviews lose their cost classification
findings.description: `requestedModel` is not an alias field: persistence emits it only on model substitution, and its value is the resolved model ID. Normal reviews therefore load with `alias=None`, preventing `cost_cell()` from identifying subscription costs as API-rate equivalents. Reproduced a subscription review displaying `$1.00 prov`. Persist and read the actual selected alias rather than repurposing `requestedModel`.

findings.title: Malformed cost basis crashes the entire reviews report
findings.description: The set-membership check assumes `costBasis` is hashable. Valid YAML such as `costBasis: [provider]` raises `TypeError`, aborting the report instead of warning and retaining the row with an unknown basis. Validate that the value is a string before membership testing, and cover list and mapping values in tests.
